question: Do the Qwen2.5-7B findings replicate in Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Gemma-2-9B-it, each using its OWN conversations? The findings are: native and pasted histories are linearly separable; a shared native-minus-pasted direction exists; adding it does not make pasted behave like native; and the direction moves answer length with its sign, including on open-ended tasks it was not built from.

gemma2.note: Gemma-2's chat template has no system role, so neither B nor C carries a system prompt

model_files: SHA256 of every downloaded weight and config file is written to model_files.json before any generation

depths.steering: k = 4, the relative depth of Qwen layer 16: llama31 layer 18, gemma2 layer 24
depths.shallow: k = 2 (llama31 9, gemma2 12): directions saved for description only; no steering at this depth in this registration

phase1_histories.cases: the 240 v2.1 candidate cases (60 per rule) in their predeclared order
phase1_histories.procedure: as v2.1: the rule text opens the first user turn, followed by three history questions; this model answers each turn greedily (cap 1024)
phase1_histories.admission: every turn ends with the end-of-turn token, contains no special token, and passes the v2.1 rule check (confirmation/common.py:check_rule, ordinary); the first 30 admitted histories per rule are used; if fewer than 30 exist the shortfall is reported and the admitted ones are used

phase2_baseline: for each admitted history and request type (ordinary, change; request text as v2.1): greedy B and C answers, rule check, and last-prompt-token states at the eight depths; ordinary also C_qa and C_json states (forward only)
phase3_directions: mean over sources of ordinary (B - C) at the steering depth, cross-fitted over 5 folds (order sha256(source_id + 'replication-v1')); random = Gaussian (torch seed 453 + source index) scaled to that source's mean norm; full-sample means at every depth

phase4_steering.site: block output at the steering depth; last prompt token and every generated token; alpha 1 (natural scale, no tuning)

phase5_open.units: the 81 open-group units of transfer v1 (open_units.jsonl, verified against the Qwen prompt IDs); user turns and final request kept, every assistant turn regenerated by this model (greedy, cap 1024)
phase5_open.vector: this model's full-sample mean at the steering depth (from phase 3, built only from the v2.1-style histories); random = Gaussian (seed 853 + unit index) scaled to its norm
phase5_open.exclusions: a unit whose prompt would exceed the model's context minus the cap is excluded and reported (relevant to Gemma-2's 8192 tokens)

length: n = generated tokens excluding the stop token (all tokens at the cap), floored at 1

primary.per_model: each model is its own replication; two primary hypotheses per model, each tested with two-sided 97.5% history-cluster bootstrap intervals (4000 resamples, numpy seed 453)

H1_length_v21.statistics: L_sign = mean log n(C_plus_mean) - log n(C_minus_mean); L_random = mean log n(C_plus_mean) - log n(C_plus_random)

secondary: probe: per depth, 5-fold (by history) standardized logistic regression and difference-of-means accuracy, ordinary and change
direction checks: leave-one-rule-out and ordinary-to-change paired sign; cos of C_qa and C_json directions with C's
behaviour: rule compliance and length of B vs C (ordinary and change)
gap closed G = 1 - KL_B(C_plus_mean)/KL_B(C), specificity indices S_random and S_sign, first-token versions
B_minus_mean vs B length; change requests analysed like H1
per-pool open results; history regeneration terminations; excluded units
comparison: Qwen2.5-7B values from intervention v1 (ordinary) and transfer v1 (open) are reported beside each model, computed with the same formulas
not_claimed: No claim beyond these three instruction-tuned models at one depth and alpha 1. Histories differ across models by design (each model's own replies), so cross-model differences in magnitude are descriptive.
